{"content": "1|# Hermes Agent - Development Guide
2|
3|This root file is a hub: what applies everywhere, then a routing table. Each area's `AGENTS.md`
4|loads automatically when you work in that directory; read it before editing there.
5|`python scripts/check` caps this file at 12k chars and every root-to-area chain at 30k: long form
6|goes in `website/docs/developer-guide/`.
7|
8|**Never give up on the right solution.**
9|
10|## What Hermes Is
11|
12|Hermes is a personal AI agent that runs one agent core across a CLI, a TUI, an Electron desktop
13|app, a web dashboard, ACP editors and a messaging gateway (25+ platform plugins). It is extended
14|through **plugins and skills**, not by growing the core.
15|
16|Two invariants shape almost every design decision and are the lens for reviewing any change:
17|
18|- **Per-conversation prompt caching is sacred.** Mutating past context, swapping toolsets,
19|  reloading memories or rebuilding the system prompt mid-conversation breaks the cached prefix and
20|  multiplies the user's cost; the ONE exception is context compression. Slash commands that change
21|  system-prompt state defer to the next session, with an opt-in `--now` (`/skills install --now`).
22|- **The core is a narrow waist; capability lives at the edges.** Every model tool is sent on
23|  every API call, so the bar for a new *core* tool is high. New capability should arrive as a
24|  CLI command + skill, a service-gated tool, or a plugin — not as core surface.
25|
26|A change to the stock system prompt or `tools[]` fails `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` until
27|`scripts/ci/prompt_surface.py render` is committed with it, and that snapshot
28|(`tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/`) needs a hermes-agent-core approval to merge.
29|
30|## Contribution rubric
31|
32|The project's intent layer, for contributors and for the triage sweeper (which may only close on
33|`implemented_on_main`, `cannot_reproduce` or `incoherent`; taste-based closes are a maintainer's
34|call, and when in doubt a PR stays open). Long form with examples:
35|`website/docs/developer-guide/contributing.md` § Contribution rubric.
36|
37|**Wanted:** real bug fixes (repro on `main`, the exact line, the whole class incl. sibling paths);
38|reach at the edges (adapters, providers, models, UI features) wired into the existing setup UX;
39|god-file → module refactors; extending before duplicating (3+ PRs in one category → an ABC +
40|orchestrator); behaviour-contract tests; E2E with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME` for
41|resolution, config, security and I/O changes; salvage by cherry-pick so authorship survives.
42|
43|**Rejected even when well-built:** hooks with no concrete consumer; new `HERMES_*` env vars for
44|non-secret config (`.env` is secrets only, behaviour goes in `config.yaml`); a new core tool when
45|terminal + file or a skill already does the job; `offset`/`limit` pagination on instructional tools;
46|"fixes" that destroy the feature they secure; outbound telemetry without an opt-in gate;
47|change-detector tests; plugins that touch core files; third-party products in the core tree (ship a
48|standalone plugin repo).
49|
50|**Before you call it a bug,** verify the claim AND the intent (`git log -p -S "<symbol>"`): the
51|isolation is often the design (profiles are islands on purpose), an absence can be load-bearing,
52|and a fix that cannot point to the line where the bug manifests has an unverified premise.
53|
54|**Security:** `SECURITY.md` is the scope authority. A §3.1 finding goes private (GitHub Security
55|Advisories or security@nousresearch.com), never into a public issue, PR, commit or comment; §3.2
56|hardening is ordinary public work. Name the §2 boundary crossed, with a repro on `main`.
57|
58|**Footprint ladder** (take the highest rung that solves it): extend existing code → CLI command +
59|skill → service-gated tool (`check_fn` answers reachability/opt-in, never per-session surface) →
60|plugin → MCP server in the catalog → new core tool (fundamental, broadly useful, unreachable
61|otherwise).
62|
63|## Development Environment
64|
65|`source ./activate` (`activate.fish`, `activate.ps1`) provisions and activates the PM environment; pick an isolated `HERMES_HOME`/`HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` first
66|(`website/docs/reference/package-management.md#developer-workflow`). Tests need the separate test
67|environment in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. **`python scripts/check`** (`just check`) runs every blocking
68|lint check CI runs, with CI's pinned tools; `--install-hook pre-push` runs it on every push (re-run
69|after pulling to refresh the hook). `just` lists every developer command (lefthook calls the same
70|recipes); a new command is a `scripts/` file plus a recipe. The `HX0xx`/`PS-P0x` rules and their
71|fixes are in `scripts/code_health/config.py`; `# noqa` does not waive a finding,
72|`# health: allow <RULE> -- <why>` does.
73|
74|## Project Struc...

{"content": "1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# Canonical test runner for hermes-agent. Run this instead of calling
3|# `pytest` directly to guarantee your local run matches CI behavior.
4|#
5|# What this script enforces:
6|#   * Per-file isolation via scripts/run_tests_parallel.py — each test
7|#     file runs in its own freshly-spawned `python -m pytest <file>`
8|#     subprocess. No xdist, no shared workers, no module-level leakage
9|#     between files.
10|#   * TZ=UTC, LANG=C.UTF-8, PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (deterministic)
11|#   * Env vars blanked (conftest.py also does this, but this
12|#     is belt-and-suspenders for anyone running pytest outside our
13|#     conftest path — e.g. on a single file)
14|#   * The checkout's test environment (via scripts/run-in-hermes-env when needed)
15|#
16|# Usage:
17|#   scripts/run_tests.sh                            # full suite
18|#   scripts/run_tests.sh -j 4                       # cap parallelism
19|#   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/               # discover only here
20|#   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/ tests/acp_adapter/    # multiple roots
21|#   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/foo.py               # single file
22|#   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/foo.py -q            # path + bare pytest flag
23|#   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/foo.py -v --tb=long  # bare flags "just work"
24|#   scripts/run_tests.sh -k 'pattern'               # value flags pass through too
25|#   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/foo.py -- --tb=long  # explicit '--' still works
26|#
27|# Bare pytest flags (anything starting with '-' that isn't one of this
28|# runner's own options: -j/--jobs, --paths, --slice, --file-timeout, etc.)
29|# are forwarded to each per-file pytest invocation automatically — no '--'
30|# separator required. The explicit '--' form still works and stacks with
31|# bare flags. Positional path arguments override the default discovery
32|# root (tests/).
33|
34|set -euo pipefail
35|
36|# ── Locate repo root ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
37|SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
38|REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
39|
40|# ── Locate python ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41|# The suite runs under the checkout's isolated test environment (pm.testenv),
42|# and only there: unless the inherited environment is current for this
43|# checkout, this script re-executes itself under scripts/run-in-hermes-env,
44|# which syncs and applies it. That holds however the script is launched
45|# (`scripts/run_tests.sh`, `bash scripts/run_tests.sh`, from CI or a shell), so
46|# a branch switch or lock edit never runs the suite against the previous
47|# dependency set.
48|#
49|# Without an activation, an explicit HERMES_PYTHON that has pytest is honored:
50|# the Nix devShell's editable venv and CI's minimal installer lanes provide
51|# one on purpose. The import check matters: a wrapped `hermes` binary exports
52|# HERMES_PYTHON pointing at a release venv without pytest.
53|_has_pytest() { [ -n "$1" ] && [ -x "$1" ] && "$1" -c 'import pytest' 2>/dev/null; }
54|# shellcheck source=scripts/_activation.sh
55|. "$SCRIPT_DIR/_activation.sh"
56|
57|# A test run under a faked HOME (worktree lanes, probe homes) provisions its
58|# test environment from the OS account's tool store instead of downloading
59|# ~1 GB of tools into every temporary home, but only while that store already
60|# records this checkout's pins (_store_has_pins). The check runs unlocked
61|# before `pm install` takes the store's install lock, so it keeps runs that
62|# START on different pins apart; it does not cover the window in between, where
63|# the account's own `hermes update` (or a run on other pins) can re-point
64|# facts.json and this run's `pm install` then re-stages its pins over them.
65|# Only this runner's own provisioning gets HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR: the pytest
66|# children below start from `env -i` without it, so tests that exercise setup,
67|# install or update resolve their own stores. Their PATH still holds the
68|# account store's tool dirs, so a test writing through a PATH tool
69|# (`pip install`, `npm -g`) would write into the account store. An explicit
70|# HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR, a custom HERMES_HOME, a home that already holds a store,
71|# or an account without a usable store keep today's per-home layout.
72|# Prints the account home, then the pinned Python minor.
73|_account_tool_store() {
74|  local account py_minor
75|  [ -z "${HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR:-}" ] || return 1
76|  case "${HERMES_HOME:-}" in "" | "$HOME/.hermes" | "$HOME/.hermes/"*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
77|  [ ! -f "$HOME/.hermes/tools/facts.json" ] || return 1
78|  account="$(getent passwd "$(id -u)" 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f6)"
79|  [ -n "$account" ] || account="$(dscl . -read "/Users/$(id -un)" NFSHomeDirectory 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^NFSHomeDirectory: *//p')"

2|"""Per-file parallel test runner.
3|
4|The minimum-viable replacement for pytest-xdist + a subprocess-isolation
5|plugin. Discovers test files under ``tests/`` (excluding integration/e2e
6|unless explicitly requested), then runs one ``python -m pytest <file>``
7|subprocess per file, with bounded parallelism (default: ``os.cpu_count()``).
8|
9|Why per-file rather than per-test?
10|    Per-test spawn overhead (~250ms × 17k tests = 70min CPU minimum)
11|    swamped the actual work. Per-file spawn (~250ms × ~850 files = ~3.5min)
12|    fits in the budget while still giving every file a fresh Python
13|    interpreter — the only isolation boundary that actually matters
14|    (cross-file module-level state leakage was the original flake source;
15|    intra-file state is the test author's responsibility).
16|
17|Why drop xdist entirely?
18|    xdist's persistent workers accumulate state across files, which is
19|    exactly the leakage we wanted to fix. xdist also adds complexity
20|    (loadfile vs loadscope, --max-worker-restart, internal control plane)
21|    that we don't need when the unit of work is "run pytest on one file".
22|    A subprocess.Popen pool gated by a semaphore is ~60 lines and does
23|    the job.
24|
25|Usage:
26|    python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py [pytest_args...]
27|
28|    Common pytest args pass through to each per-file pytest invocation
29|    (e.g. ``-q``, ``-v``, ``-x``, ``--tb=long``, ``-k 'pattern'``, ``--lf``)
30|    with no special separator — a bare ``-q`` "just works". Anything after
31|    a literal ``--`` is also passed through, and stacks with bare flags.
